## Course Setup

| Item | Setting |
|:------------|:--------------------------------------|
| Course | 語音處理與人機互動 · Speech Processing and Human-Machine Interaction |
| Audience | Master's / PhD students |
| Prerequisites | None required; linear algebra, probability and Python are soft expectations |
| Format | 14 weeks × 3 hours, lectures throughout |
| Assessment | None |
| Compute | Free-tier Colab (T4, 16 GB) |
| Language | Lectures in Mandarin, slides in English |
| Depth | Graduate — derivations, the literature behind each idea, open problems |

::: {.callout-note}
## On "no prerequisites" together with "full derivations"
The two are in tension, and the course accepts that deliberately. The catch-up load is concentrated in the second half of W2 (signals and representation) and the first half of W3 (a fast review of HMMs), and week 1 hands out a two-page list of the mathematics assumed: inner products and projection from linear algebra, conditional independence and marginalization from probability, and gradient descent. W3, W6 and W8 are the three mathematical peaks; each needs an hour or more at the board.
:::

## Course Structure

| Part | Weeks | Content |
|:-----------|:---------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Part I — Foundations** | W1–W6 | Systems view and the latency budget; signals and the front end; alignment (HMM → CTC); Transformers and streaming; SSL representation learning; neural codecs and discretization |
| **Part II — Modules** | W7–W10 | ASR; TTS generative paradigms; TTS controllability and evaluation; the acoustic front end (VAD / AEC / enhancement / separation / speaker) |
| **Part III — Dialogue Systems** | W11–W14 | Audio-native LMs (half-duplex); modeling turn-taking; full-duplex architectures and data; evaluation and deployment |

W6 — neural codecs and tokenization — is the hinge of the course: W11–W14 rest entirely on frame rate, token budget, and the separation of semantic from acoustic information.
